$comment: The shared Arabic / RTL qualification contract. Both the Python suite (servers/fastapi/tests/qualification/test_arabic_rtl_qualification.py) and the TypeScript suite (servers/nextjs/tests/arabic-rtl-qualification.test.mjs) read this one table, so the two classifiers are checked against one declaration instead of two copies.

evidence_classes.model: The classification of the text itself. Measured in both languages.
evidence_classes.markup: The contract the renderer emits. Measured in the markup, not in rendered pixels.
evidence_classes.rendered: Rendered pixels. NOT measured by this suite: no headless browser is available in servers/nextjs/tests.

cases.assertion: The element declares a base direction and the font stack names an Arabic-capable family.
The regression guard: the font stack still leads with the design font, and the text is emitted verbatim.
One container, no inner dir, no run splitting: the browser's bidi algorithm owns the reordering.
Both numeral systems survive byte-for-byte, and the Arabic-Indic digits are not normalised.
The table cell declares its own base direction.
The chart label text survives verbatim. Chart rendering is canvas-based; the label's rendered order is NOT asserted.
The vector text survives verbatim. Vector text is laid out by an LTR segment engine in the canvas; the rendered order is NOT asserted.
The speaker note survives verbatim. A speaker note is not a rendered text element, so it is not containment-checked.
Each cell resolves its own direction; the row does not force one direction on the other.
Diacritics survive byte-for-byte and no bidi control characters are injected into the output.
